newsitem.title: USA: CBOT soymeal ends higher on bean gains, China talk.
newsitem.headline: CBOT soymeal ends higher on bean gains, China talk.

text.p: A rally in soybean futures coupled with rumors China continues to buy U.S. soymeal, boosted CBOT soymeal futures to a higher close, traders said.
Soyoil also closed higher on China talk with a drawdown in soyoil stocks despite aggressive U.S. soybean crushings, buoying prices.
"There are China rumors, rumors they're looking to buy more meal and oil," said Vic Lespinasse of Dean Witter Reynolds.
Traders said commercial buying boosted soymeal plus Refco Inc was a noted purchaser of the December contract.
"Refco bought it and crushers are buying it. The ADM, Cargill and Continental-types," a trader said.
Soymeal was led higher by gains in the nearby months.
Fears of tight nearby supplies boosted seller prices for South American soymeal pellets $2.00 to $5.00 per tonne.
Soymeal closed $0.50 to $4.60 per ton higher, with December up $4.60 at $238.90 per ton.
Soyoil closed 0.06 to 0.15 cent per lb higher, with December up 0.10 at 23.63.
Cargill Inc bought 400 lots of January soyoil, traders said.

"There is little unsold soymeal arriving into Europe at the moment and crushers here (Rotterdam) also do not run at full capacity yet as arrivals of beans were late this year. Therefore nearby material is tight and prices for those postions soar," one Rotterdam-based broker said.
The recovery in soyoil was tied to a rally in soybeans and rumors that China was in the market for U.S. soyoil and meal.
Traders said the market was impressed with a drawdown in soyoil stocks during October despite an aggressive soybean crush pace.

The National Oilseed Processors Assocation (NOPA) October crush report showed soy crushings during October at 125.601 million bushels, up from 99.300 million in September and above the 120.005 million crushed during October of 1995.
Soyoil stocks at the end of October stood at 1.742 billion lbs, down from 1.761 billion in September but above 482.171 million in October a year ago.
October soymeal exports totaled 706,932 tons, up from 288,089 tons in September and above the 500,788 tons exported in October of 1995.
Technicians said key moving averages for soymeal and soyoil were beginning to give off bullish flags.
First resistance in December soymeal futures was $236.97 a ton and second resistance was $241.87. The session high for December was $239.00 a ton.
In December soyoil, first resistance was 23.68 cents a lb and second resistance was 24.07 cents. The session high for December was 23.72.
Soymeal futures volume was estimated at 26,000, down from 28,037 Friday, according to the CBOT. Soyoil futures volume was estimated at 22,000, down from 28,450 Friday.
